name: Allegheny County tree canopy 2020 (Tree Pittsburgh and the University of Vermont, on PASDA)
method: Tree canopy variable and canopy map in Explore; Sun, shade and trees on the Place page. Canopy area inside each area divided by its land area (scripts/16_build_canopy.py; docs/data/canopy.md).
caveats: Published as a 2015-2020 change file without its change classes; its extent matches the 2020 canopy Tree Pittsburgh reports. Power lines and building edges can read as canopy. Display only, never scored.

name: PHFA Qualified Allocation Plan, selection criteria: 2025/2026 and the 2027/2028 draft
geography: statewide rules; Pittsburgh is in the urban pool
method: Tax credit score sheet on the Place page. Points, tiers and caps transcribed by hand into app/src/data/lazy/lihtc_pa.json and added up as entered (docs/data/lihtc.md).
caveats: A self-score: PHFA scores every application itself, and the draft can change. Which lines the place decides is this project's reading.

name: ACS 5-year 2020-2024: renter households by size, age and income, the homes they rent and their rents (Census API)
geography: city tracts, the city's ZCTAs, the city
method: Who needs it on the Place page. B25009 (tenure by household size), B25042 (tenure by bedrooms), B25068 (bedrooms by gross rent), B25118 (tenure by income), B25119 (median income by tenure), B25032 (tenure by units in structure), B25007 (tenure by age of householder), B25064; labels checked against the API's variable list before use. Shares carry the ACS proportion margin of error; signals count only past a printed mark and the margin of error (scripts/17_build_demand.py; docs/data/demand.md).
caveats: Tract margins are wide, so a signal falls back to the tract's ZIP code (the whole ZCTA, part of which may lie outside the city). Household size and home size describe the same occupied homes: a gap says how renters are housed, not that homes are missing. Display and ordering only, never scored.

name: HUD Low-Income Housing Tax Credit property database (public ArcGIS layer)
vintage: as published by HUD (placed in service through the file's latest year)
method: Tax credit homes in each tract, within a mile of it and in each ZIP code, by year placed in service; the nearest properties to each tract's center. Property fields only: never the contact, company or telephone fields (scripts/17_build_demand.py).
caveats: HUD's file lags new awards by a year or more. The 30-year mark (15-year compliance plus 15 years of extended use) is an assumption: properties placed before 1990 had less, and some carry longer terms.

name: City of Pittsburgh Zoning Code, Title Nine (eCode360)
method: What can be built on the Place page. Development subdistrict standards (§903.03), mixed-use district standards (§904.01-§904.04), the Use Table (§911.02), the ADU overlay rule (§912.08), parking minimums (§914.02) and the inclusionary overlay (§907.04.A), transcribed by hand into config/zoning_standards.json with each row's section; applied to every city lot and summed to tracts (scripts/18_build_zoning_capacity.py; docs/data/zoning_capacity.md).
caveats: A reading of the code, not a zoning determination. Contextual setbacks and heights (§925.06, §925.07), compatibility standards (Chapter 916), slopes, parking and variances are not modeled; envelope districts use assumed home sizes. Districts set by height maps, downtown, riverfront and planned districts are not computed. The older by-right table in config/zoning_rules.json stays marked unverified.

name: City of Pittsburgh Inclusionary Housing Overlay District (ArcGIS feature layer)
method: Share of each tract inside the IZ-O (2,457 acres: Bloomfield, the three Lawrencevilles, Polish Hill and parts of Oakland); the 10% set-aside of §907.04.A is applied to projects of 20 or more homes where most of the tract is inside.
caveats: The overlay is tested by tract share, not by site: a site near its edge needs the City's map.

name: HUD FY2026 Multifamily Tax Subsidy Project (MTSP) income limits, Pittsburgh HMFA (HUD User API)
method: Tax credit rents in the pencil on the Place page: 30% of the limit at 1.5 persons a bedroom (a studio counts one person, a half person takes the mean of the neighboring limits) ÷ 12, rounded down, less the utility allowance (scripts/19_build_pencil_defaults.py; docs/data/pencil.md).
caveats: MTSP limits, not the Section 8 limits the rest of the Place page uses; the two agree at 50% here and differ by a few dollars at 30% and 80%. No HERA special limits apply to the Pittsburgh area.

name: Housing Authority of the City of Pittsburgh, 2026 Housing Choice Voucher utility allowance schedule
method: Default utility allowance in the pencil: low-rise apartment (4 stories or fewer), standard, tenant paying electric heat pump heating, electric cooking, other electric, air conditioning and electric water heating; owner paying water, sewer and trash ($111, $133, $171, $210 for studio to 3 bedrooms).
caveats: One of several allowance methods a tax credit project may use; the right one depends on the building's utilities and PHFA's rules. Editable on the card.
